subject.title: fix(security): add ReDoS guard to exec approval argPattern matching

question: Should legacy exec-approval argPatterns with unsafe nested repetition fail closed while every accepted pattern retains its exact stored text semantics?
rationale: This changes persisted command-approval outcomes: rejection improves resilience, but normalization can broaden authorization and unconditional rejection can break existing operator policies, so the permanent boundary must be maintainer-approved.

options.title: Reject unsafe, preserve exact text
options.body: Validate without normalization, compile the original accepted pattern, and treat unsafe nested repetition as a non-match with focused compatibility coverage.

options.title: Normalize approval patterns
options.body: Explicitly adopt trimmed regex semantics as a breaking approval-policy change with migration, documentation, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Defer the hardening
options.body: Keep current matching behavior until a broader regex-policy and migration contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Reject unsafe, preserve exact text
recommendation.body: Validate without normalization, compile the original accepted pattern, and treat unsafe nested repetition as a non-match with focused compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent repository security and exec-policy ownership makes this the best available routing candidate for the trust-model and compatibility decision.
